  - Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video and may request to speak using the

  which item on the agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the
  City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agenda

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 6, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A special meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 5:05 p.m. via teleconference by VICE CHAIR BAIN.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  VICE CHAIR BAIN led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Persichina, Romanelli, McCormick, Pope,
  and Retz

  Commissioners Absent:  Ciarolla

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

  Also Present:  Councilmember Stegura and Environmental
  Advisory Committee Member Navi Uppal

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST
  15, 2022

  Approval of the minutes was tabled to the September 19, 2022 Park and Activities
  Commission meeting.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
September 6, 2022
   A.  TURF REPLACEMENT PROJECT FINAL DESIGN AND COST PROPOSAL

  Assistant City Manager Davis gave a brief overview of the written report with
  additional information provided by Superintendent Goldsmith. Superintendent
  Goldsmith added that there would be no issue with staff participating with some of
  the planting at the start of the project.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if staff participation would offset the cost. Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that it would not and was intended to provide staff with an
  opportunity to participate. Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis explained that staff
  participation was meant to be a fun service activity to kick-off the planting for staff
  and any Commission or Committee members wanting to participate in the project.

  ACM Davis noted that staff had worked closely with California Water Services (Cal
  Water) and the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC) on the project
  adding that Cris Sarabia of PVPLC provided a list of recommended plants which
  are drought tolerant and native. She stated some plants would be purchased from
  the PVPLC and that signage would be included to let visitors know that PVPLC sells
  these plants as part of the established demonstration garden.

  COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA who serves as the Chair of the Environmental
  Advisory Committee (EAC) added that the landscape design firm is intentionally
  choosing plants that will spread once established, which will reduce the number of
  plants needed and help keep the budget down.

  ACM Davis noted that items discussed at the August Commission meeting had
  been addressed and are incorporated into the final plans. She added that the
  demonstration garden is a key component to be located at City Hall, and that the
  demonstration feature at Highridge will include natural drainage features. ACM
  Davis noted that shading for the bigger decomposed granite area outside City Hall
  did not get formally incorporated into the plan and is still being discussed. She also
  noted that the irrigation systems would be updated, and that Superintendent
  Goldsmith would be working with Bennett Landscaping noting the irrigation would
  be updated to a drip-type system.

  In response to COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Superintendent Goldsmith stated
  the budget was initially over budget but had been brought down. Superintendent
  Goldsmith stated that costs were lowered by reducing the number of valves needed
  by using some existing valves and going with a different brand of timers and flow
  sensors, from high-end to low-end while still being able to have efficiencies and
  controls.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
September 6, 2022
   COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there was a negotiation with Bennett
  regarding their proposal. Superintendent Goldsmith responded affirmatively adding
  there were multiple conversations with Bennett to get the costs down.

  ACM Davis noted that the negotiations were mainly handled by Superintendent
  Goldsmith in response to COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, adding that there might
  be opportunity out in the field for plant size changes as well as potential savings
  working with the PVPLC.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked what type of arrangement there would be
  with Bennett other than their existing contract. ACM Davis responded that Bennett
  had provided specifications and proposals for both sites as special projects under
  the current contract.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI thanked Superintendent Goldsmith for his work on
  the project.

  COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA thanked Superintendent Goldsmith and staff noting
  there was a very short timeline to get this done to be eligible for the grant. She
  added that while Cal Water had been accommodating, staff worked quickly. She
  additionally thanked ACM Davis and City Manager Grammer and expressed
  appreciation to the Environmental Advisory Committee for their time reviewing the
  project. COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA noted that City Council reviewed the
  concept at its previous meeting and was looking for the Park and Activities
  Commission’s recommendation to move forward.

  EAC COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL asked if the project would interfere with the
  installation of electric vehicle (EV) chargers at Highridge Park. Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that it would not impact the installation of EV chargers as the
  project is at the back of the park.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked ACM Davis to comment about the difficulty of installing
  EV chargers at Highridge Park. ACM Davis noted that at the moment Highridge and
  Ernie Howlett are not feasible locations for EV chargers until more funding is
  available, adding that staff is on the lookout for grants that can support the
  necessary infrastructure needed to install them in the future.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if the number of plants designated in the City Hall drawing
  were needed and/or beneficial as plants that would spread were being purchased.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he would work with the landscape designer
  and contractor.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN commented about the number of plants being provided by
  PVPLC. ACM Davis stated that she did not believe PVPLC would be able to provide

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
September 6, 2022
   all of the plants needed. Superintendent Goldsmith noted that Tree of Life is another
  source for plants.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the current water shutoff would affect the
  planting. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that time would be needed to
  prepare the site so the shutoff should have no impact the project.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ shared that he is aware of a someone who grows natural,
  drought tolerant plants locally whose information he could share. He noted he may
  already be connected with the PVPLC but if not could be an additional source for
  plants. COMMISSIONER RETZ also congratulated staff for being able to get the
  budget down to the amount provided by the rebate. Superintendent Goldsmith
  asked COMMISSIONER RETZ to pass the contact information to him stating he
  could share the information with Cris Sarabia so they could collaborate with his
  contact.

  EAC COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL asked about the warm-up and waiting areas
  on the City Hall drawing. ACM Davis stated that some visitors prefer to wait outside
  when waiting for an appointment at City Hall and that there is an existing patio
  outside the Council Chambers that would be an extension of that area making it
  more accessible. ACM DAVIS noted that also students often meet up in the warm-
  up area to stretch and then run on the trails. ACM Davis said the thought was to
  make it an inviting and easy space to gather and stretch. VICE CHAIR BAIN
  clarified that the area towards PV Drive North is the warm-up area and the waiting
  area is set but not a fully developed concept yet. COUNCILMEMBER STEGURA
  added that the area will be sparse for the time being with the idea that seating will
  be added later.. VICE CHAIR BAIN commented that it is a reimagining of the space
  which will allow more room to gather compared to gathering on a narrow path. She
  added it will be a great enhancement and although it will not be built out at the
  completion of this project it will be done in the future.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK
  to:

  ADOPT THE PLANS AND THE BENNETT LANDSCAPING PROPOSAL AS
  SUBMITTED AND RECOMMEND APPROVAL BY CITY COUNCIL.

  AYES: McCormick, Persichina, Retz, Romanelli, Pope, Bain
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: Ciarolla

  The motion carried.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
September 6, 2022
   VICE CHAIR BAIN shared information about the upcoming City Celebration and
  shared that volunteers were still needed for the ticket sales booth.
